tagline: Helping people live healthier lives and helping make the health system work better for everyone
hero_kpi_rationale: Optum is UNH's strategic growth engine, combining health services, data, and technology to create a durable advantage in modernizing the health system. Its growth outpaces UnitedHealthcare and reflects the shift toward an integrated model.

kpis.name: Optum Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by Optum's technology, pharmacy, and care delivery operations.
kpis.description: Optum includes Optum Health, Optum Rx, and Optum Insight. This segment benefits from vertical integration and the rising adoption of value-based care services.
kpis.signal: Sustained double-digit growth despite macro pressures.

kpis.name: UnitedHealthcare Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from health insurance premiums collected by UnitedHealthcare.
kpis.description: UNH's legacy segment, covering employer, Medicare, and Medicaid markets. A major revenue source despite regulatory and pricing pressures.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by higher premiums and membership increases.

kpis.name: Adjusted Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit as a percentage of total revenue, excluding special items and restructuring impacts.
kpis.description: Margin was affected by medical costs exceeding expectations (19% growth vs. expectations), 2025 restructuring charges, and losses in value-based care.
kpis.signal: Significant margin compression due to elevated medical costs and restructuring actions.

kpis.name: Medical Cost Trend
kpis.explanation: Annual increase in unit costs and utilization of medical care relative to pricing assumptions.
kpis.description: Medical costs rose 19% in 2025 (source 10-K: medical costs grew 19%), significantly surpassing pricing assumptions and expected inflation. This divergence is driven by higher service intensity, health status of new enrollees, and Medicare Advantage impacts.
kpis.signal: Critical cost pressure: actual trend well above pricing expectations, particularly in behavioral health, pharmacy, and home care.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after operating and capital expenditures.
kpis.description: UNH generated $19.7 billion in operating cash flow in 2025, supported by the scale of its integrated operations despite operational challenges and restructuring impacts.
kpis.signal: Cash generation impacted by restructurings and special charges, but remains substantial.

kpis.name: Number of People in Value-Based Care
kpis.explanation: Number of patients managed under care models where Optum is financially accountable for outcomes.
kpis.description: This model is central to Optum Health's strategy, but faces pressure from Medicare funding and high medical costs. Expected contraction in 2026 due to rate increases in response to anticipated cost trends and declining Medicare Advantage enrollment.
kpis.signal: First contraction after years of growth, reflecting Medicare pressures and elevated medical costs.

kpis.name: Direct Costs Related to Cyberattack
kpis.explanation: Provisions for provider loans and losses related to the February 21, 2024, attack on Change Healthcare.
kpis.description: The February 2024 attack led to significant provisions. In Q4 2025, the Company increased its reserves by $799 million for expected net recoveries associated with provider loans and other customer balances, recorded in operating costs and attributable to Optum Insight.
kpis.signal: Significant impact from a one-time event on operating costs, reserves recorded in Q4 2025.

kpis.name: 2025 Restructuring Costs
kpis.explanation: Costs related to real estate rationalization, workforce reductions, contract reassignments, and provisions for future losses.
kpis.description: In Q4 2025, UNH launched a $2.5 billion restructuring plan including: real estate optimization and headcount reductions ($746 million), contract reassignments ($573 million), reserves for expected 2026 value-based care losses ($623 million), securities revaluation losses ($329 million), and funding advance to United Health Foundation ($250 million).
kpis.signal: Major strategic action to refocus the company on core businesses and improve profitability.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

kpis.name: Medical Cost Trend
kpis.explanation: Augmentation annuelle des coûts unitaires et de l'utilisation des soins médicaux.
kpis.description: Medical costs increased 18.85% in 2025 (313,995M$ vs 264,185M$ in 2024), substantially outpacing rate expectations and anticipated inflation. This divergence stems from increased service intensity, health profile of newly enrolled members, and Medicare Advantage impacts. MD&A states: pricing trends and patient assumptions were well-short of the medical cost trends incurred.
kpis.signal: Critical cost pressure: performance significantly exceeding rate expectations, notably in behavioral care and related segments.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Bénéfice opérationnel par rapport au revenu total.
kpis.description: Margin was pressured by medical costs exceeding expectations (18.85% growth), 2.5 Bn$ restructuring provisions in 2025, and shared-risk care arrangement losses. Earnings from operations 19,012M$ on revenues 447,567M$.
kpis.signal: Significant margin compression driven by elevated medical costs and restructuring charges.

kpis.name: UnitedHealthcare Premiums
kpis.explanation: Revenus provenant des primes d'assurance santé collectées par UnitedHealthcare.
kpis.description: UNH's legacy segment covering employer, Medicare and Medicaid markets. Major revenue source despite regulatory and rate pressures. Growth of 43.4 Bn$ driven by Medicare Advantage and rate adjustments in response to elevated medical costs.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by premium increases and covered lives expansion.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Trésorerie générée par les opérations après dépenses d'exploitation.
kpis.description: UNH generated 19.7 Bn$ in operating cash flow in 2025, down from 23.6 Bn$ in 2024. Decline reflects impacts of elevated medical costs, restructurings and cybersecurity provisions, while maintaining robust cash generation.
kpis.signal: Cash generation impacted by restructuring and exceptional charges, yet remains substantial.

kpis.name: Domestic People Served
kpis.explanation: Nombre total de personnes servies par UnitedHealthcare aux États-Unis.
kpis.description: UnitedHealthcare served 415,000 additional people in 2025, driven by fee-based commercial and Medicare Advantage. MD&A indicates expected Medicare Advantage contraction in 2026 following rate adjustments and profit normalization.
kpis.signal: Modest growth driven by Medicare Advantage and fee-based commercial, offset by Medicaid attrition.

risks.title: Medical Cost Estimation Risk
risks.score_rationale: This risk is highlighted in the 10-K, represents approximately 80% of revenues, and employs strong language (materially and adversely affect). It is central to the health insurance business model. Industrial category is heavily weighted here.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Data Protection
risks.score_rationale: Risk is detailed extensively, with reference to actual 2024 incident at Change Healthcare. Language is alarming (compromises, costly recovery). Healthcare data dependence makes this critical.

risks.title: Information Systems Dependency
risks.score_rationale: Risk is well positioned in the document, with mention of generative AI and system integration. Language is concerned but less urgent than existential risks. Technology category is important but less weighted than Industrial.

risks.title: Strained Provider Relationships
risks.score_rationale: Risk is clearly exposed, with threats to profitability and network access. Language is preventive but repeated. Competition category is moderately weighted.

risks.title: Evolving Data and AI Regulation
risks.score_rationale: Risk is explicitly linked to AI and data, with mention of changing requirements across United States and international jurisdictions. Language is cautious but emphasizes uncertainty. Regulatory category is significant in healthcare sector.

risks.title: Liability for Provider Failure
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned in context of shared-risk arrangements. Language is measured, but indirect financial loss risk is real. Credit category is less critical here.

ai_positioning.summary: UnitedHealth Group uses AI and data analytics to optimize care, improve clinical outcomes, and reduce costs. AI is embedded in Optum Insight for predictive analytics and in Optum Health for population health management, but positioning remains one of progressive adoption rather than AI innovation leadership.
